properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 3 at 8:44AM MST until November 3 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Havasu Creek basin in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona. This includes the
Colorado River between river miles 157 and 158...

* Until 300 PM MST Tuesday.

* At 844 AM MST, A river gauge on Cataract Creek below Heather Wash
reported a rapid rise of 2.7 feet. This rise is due to runoff from
heavy rain that occurred on previous days. Flash flooding is
already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding is anticipated in the Havasu Creek basin.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding is anticipated in the Havasu Creek basin.

* For Cataract Creek at Cataract Creek Below Heather Wash:
At 6:30am the stage was 6.98 feet.
Flood Stage is 7.5 feet.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: 450 cfs flow. May cause minor flooding downstream in
Supai campground 4 to 7 hours later.
At 10.0 feet: 1520 cfs flow. May cause moderate flooding downstream
in Suapi villago 4 to 7 hours later.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Supai, Havasupai Reservation, Little Navajo Falls, Mooney Falls and
Beaver Falls.

This includes the Colorado River between river miles 157 and 158.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Very Last Chance Camp Site.

This includes the following swimming holes...
All swimming holes on Havasu Creek near Supai.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River, Havasu Creek, Coconino Wash, Black Tank Wash,
Pasture Wash, Sinyella Canyon, Little Coyote Canyon and Heather
Wash.
properties.instruction:
Campers and hikers should hustle to higher ground immediately! Stay
away from creeks and washes!

Foot bridges will be washed out in Supai Campground. Some campsites
will be flooded. Campers may be stranded in portions of the
campground.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 8:20AM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues along the
San Juan River from near Bluff to the terminus at Lake Powell.

* WHERE...Southwestern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 813 AM MST, stream gauge reports indicates the observed stage
on the San Juan River at Bluff has exceeded flood stage and is at
23.7 feet. Timing of additional crests is subject to change as
more details become available. Please continue to monitor the
forecast and updated  warnings.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
the San Juan River from Bluff to the terminus at Lake Powell.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 3 at 6:35AM PST by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
Patchy dense fog has been observed in the Walla Walla Valley early
this morning. Within fog, visibilities of one-quarter mile or
less are expected to persist into mid-morning. Use extra caution
while traveling as visibilities can change quickly. If fog is
encountered, use low-beam headlights and keep plenty of space
between you and other vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Rio Arriba, NM
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 7:35AM MST until November 3 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 AM MST Tuesday the stage was 6.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:00 AM MST Tuesday was 6.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
this afternoon and continue falling through tonight and
Wednesday.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.1
feet on 07/26/2001.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 500 PM MST.

Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 6:02AM MST until November 3 at 10:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 558 AM MST, water levels near Woodruff and Holbrook have
fallen below flood stage with no additional rises expected. Water
levels at Winslow remain above moderate flood stage, and
additional rises to above major flood stage will be possible
through the day today. Flooding will continue to remain a threat
downstream of Winslow in the Birdsprings area as well. Flooding
is already ongoing.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 5:00am MST the stage was 23.18 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Additional rises over 25.0 feet are possible through
the day.
Impacts:
At 22.0 feet: Lowland flooding on right bank. Damage on left bank
to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in the event of levee failure.
At 25.0 feet: Levee is overtopped. Major flooding of portions of
Winslow including Ames Acres and Bushman Acres.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Winslow, Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres, Homolovi
Ruins State Park and Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large

rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

forecast.

properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:53PM MST until November 4 at 4:00PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River continues.

* WHAT...Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River,
caused by recent runoff from upstream rain and snowmelt, is
occurring.

* WHERE...Eastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
West Central Costilla County in south central Colorado...
South Central Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Conejos River, from Mogote downstream
to Manassa, and the San Antonio River, near Ortiz downstream to
Manassa, is ongoing. Additional flooding of creeks, streams, and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations is possible. Numerous
roads remain closed due to flooding. Expect many areas of slow
moving or standing water through eastern Conejos County.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 347 PM MST, Upstream runoff from recent rain and snowmelt is
causing flooding into eastern Conejos County.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford, Antonito, Romeo, Alamosa East, Conejos and
Ortiz.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:31PM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the San Juan River caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...along the San Juan River from the Four Corners through
Mexican Hat, UT. This includes Bluff, Montezuma Creek and Aneth.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM MST, stream gauge reports upstream and impacts of
flooding have been reported along the San Juan River near
Farmington, NM. Expect flood waters to reach the Four Corners
Wednesday evening and the town of Bluff early Thursday morning.
Timing of crest is subject to change as more details become
available. Please continue to monitor the forecast and updated
warnings.
- At 11:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 22 feet late this evening with
a secondary crest near 23.5 feet expected near Bluff early
Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Bluff, Montezuma Creek, and Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
